extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word if exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word. The dataset exemplifies a wide range of linguistic phenomena and is designed to challenge models to understand broader discourse context.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.publisher: CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento; Institute for Logic, Language & Computation, University of Amsterdam
extraction.citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. arXiv preprint arXiv:1606.06031.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The LAMBADA dataset was constructed from the Book Corpus, which contains unpublished novels. The corpus was filtered to remove duplicates and potentially offensive material. Passages were selected based on specific criteria: the target word had to be guessable from the broader context but not from the last sentence alone. This involved filtering out passages where standard language models assigned a high probability to the target word. Human subjects were then used to validate the passages through a crowdsourcing pipeline, ensuring strict criteria for inclusion.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data comes from the Book Corpus, which includes 5,325 novels and 465 million words. The corpus was filtered to remove duplicates and potentially offensive material using a stop word list.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The corpus was filtered to remove duplicates and potentially offensive material using a stop word list. Passages were further filtered based on the probability assigned by language models to the target word, excluding those with a probability greater than 0.00175.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects were used to validate the passages through a crowdsourcing pipeline. The process involved three steps: (1) guessing the target word based on the whole passage, (2) a second subject guessing the target word based on the whole passage, and (3) subjects guessing the target word based on the target sentence only. Passages were included in the dataset only if two consecutive subjects matched the missing word exactly and no subject could guess it from the local context alone.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process ensured that the target word was guessable from the broader context but not from the last sentence alone. The criteria for inclusion were strict, requiring two consecutive subjects to match the missing word exactly and ensuring no subject could guess it from the local context alone.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple annotations per item were collected, with an average cost of $1.24 per item. The process involved up to 10 subjects per item in the crowdsourcing pipeline.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language models (pre-trained RNN, 4-gram model, RNN, and feed-forward model) were used to filter passages based on the probability assigned to the target word.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is intended to be used as a benchmark for evaluating language models. The development set and training corpus are available for download, and the test set will be made available at the time of a planned public competition.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset contains a bias towards proper nouns, which are overrepresented (48% of target words). The target words are often strongly cued in the broader discourse, with over 80% of LAMBADA passages including the target word in the context.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to narrative passages from novels and may not generalize to other text genres. The strict filtering criteria may limit the diversity of the dataset. The dataset is designed to challenge models to understand broader discourse context, which may not reflect typical language modeling tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is intended to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding, particularly their ability to take broader discourse context into account when predicting a word.
